evidence: Read the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx with openpyxl: Quality Checks row 53 (check 52) requires no live credentials, real personal data, host paths, unpinned remote fetch or injection payload; Internal Quality Checks row 53 annotates deliberate task.toml integration credentials as delivery-time stripping. Applied frozen Harbor SKILL.md Known false positives / Delivery profile and references/quality-checks.md:208-210, alongside qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md. Independently SHA256-verified all 50 task files and every frozen rule against manifest.json; zero mismatches. Read/scanned every task file, including the hidden tests/.dockerignore, full lockfile, vendor source and compiled frontend, rather than only the brief or server. Candidate scans found zero recognizable live-key/private-key material, author-machine paths or prompt-injection language, and no literal remote fetch/script/import command. Credential-assignment matches were only task.toml:34-35: ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN = "${OPENROUTER_API_KEY}" and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = ""; these are the prescribed variable reference and empty fallback, not shipped credentials. Runtime tokens are generated per run by crypto.randomUUID() (solution/app/src/runtime.ts:195-196,249) and checked with the active frame source (260), not personal or provider credentials. The sole email is environment/Dockerfile:20, turing@local.invalid, the synthetic git identity. Seed environment/assets/seed_data.json:2-4 contains product metadata and snippets: []; instruction.md:1 and environment/instructions/policy.md:3 explicitly specify no accounts. All other authored example/test identities inspected are synthetic snippet names/markers, with no personal records. Container paths /app, /assets, /instructions, /tests and /root are required runtime paths, not author-host paths. Download review: solution/app/package.json:14-19 uses exact dependency versions; all 168 resolved entries in its 169-entry package-lock packages table have registry.npmjs.org versioned tarball URLs and sha512 integrity. solution/solve.sh:25-26 removes only the specified database files and copies the local bundled app, with no download/install. Both Dockerfiles, tests/test.sh and both tests/tools files are byte-identical to the frozen template; environment/Dockerfile:9-11 and tests/Dockerfile:16-21,31 pin directly installed npm/Python versions. Template apt operations and supported image tags were assessed under the documented Docker/profile override, not silently hardened. Other URL hits are localhost probes, DOM namespace strings, React error documentation, prescribed OpenRouter configuration, and the locally intercepted synthetic network probes in tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:37-46,204. They are not arbitrary unpinned task fetches. Browser assets/CDNs are explicitly permitted by the frozen public-network profile. Security-test snippets and intentional broken/looping examples are bounded product fixtures, not instructions to override the grader: the functional prompt:1 treats submitted content as untrusted product evidence and :7 prohibits source inspection/patches and unbounded attacks. server.js:37,61,72-73,84-85 stores source via parameterized SQL; source is not evaluated server-side. No credible row-52 defect was found. This is source inspection and read-only scan evidence; no claim is made about a hosted checker, judge run, Oracle score, or exhaustive runtime sandbox proof.
counterexample: False-fail witness actually present: task.toml:34 contains an AUTH_TOKEN assignment that a generic secret-key regex flags, but parsing the value shows the canonical ${OPENROUTER_API_KEY} reference, not a credential. Likewise runtime.ts:249 creates a fresh message-correlation token, so the word token is insufficient evidence. A plausible false-pass is a provider-key assignment hidden only in solution/app/src/vendor.js or a built public asset while a reviewer checks only instruction.md/seed/task.toml. The all-50-file scan includes both those files. A bounded in-memory review-method control with synthetic `const api_key = 'review-fixture-only-not-a-live-credential';` produced a credential-assignment candidate for manual review; it was never written into the task and was not misreported as a live secret. No current defective implementation witness was found.
